html:
On 23 March 1996 Taiwan held its first direct election for president, the first time a Chinese speaking society chose its head of state by popular vote. The sitting president, Lee Teng-hui, won with 54 per cent.

Lee, the first Taiwan-born president, had followed Chiang Ching-kuo in 1988 and dismantled the old system step by step. The People's Republic of China saw him as a secret supporter of independence and fired missiles into the sea near Taiwan's ports before the vote, in the Third Taiwan Strait Crisis. The United States sent two aircraft carrier groups.

The threats backfired and boosted Lee's vote. In 2000 the opposition won the presidency, the fruit of the Kaohsiung incident generation. Elections have changed the ruling party peacefully several times since, while Beijing still claims the island.
sum: On 23 March 1996 Taiwan held its first direct election for president, the first time a Chinese speaking society chose its head of state by popular vote. The sitting president, Lee Teng-hui, won with 54 per cent.
